source_text: Vix enim pro iusto quis moritur; nam pro bono forsitan quis audeat mori. Commendat autem Deus caritatem suam in nobis, quoniam si, cum adhuc peccatores essemus, Christus pro nobis mortuus est, multo magis iustificati nunc in sanguine ipsius salvi erimus per eum ab ira. Si enim cum inimici essemus, reconciliati sumus Deo per mortem Filii eius, multo magis reconciliati salvi erimus in vita eius. Non solum autem hoc, sed et gloriantes in Deo per Dominum nostrum Iesum Christum, per quem nunc reconciliationem accepimus [n260] . Aperuit, quanta totum Christus pietate gessisset, qui mori dignatus est pro nihil boni merentibus.
pass_a_gloss: For scarcely does anyone die for a just person; for perhaps someone may dare to die for a good person. But God commends his love in us, because if, when we were still sinners, Christ died for us, much more, justified now in his blood, we will be saved through him from wrath. For if when we were enemies we were reconciled to God through the death of his Son, much more, reconciled, we will be saved in his life. Not only however this, but also glorying in God through our Lord Jesus Christ, through whom we have now received reconciliation. He opened with how great a piety Christ had carried the whole, who deigned to die for those meriting nothing of good.

lemmas.lexica: LS iustificatio; Blaise forensic making-just, not later system
LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS mors; Blaise temporal vs eternal death in Rom 5

pass_b_english: ‘For scarcely does anyone die for a righteous person, though perhaps someone would dare to die for a good person. But God commends his love toward us because, if Christ died for us while we were still sinners, much more, now justified in his blood, shall we be saved through him from wrath. For if, while we were enemies, we were reconciled to God through the death of his Son, much more, once reconciled, shall we be saved in his life. And not only this, but we also glory in God through our Lord Jesus Christ, through whom we have now received reconciliation’ (Romans 5:7–11). He has revealed the great compassion with which Christ did everything: he deigned to die for people who deserved nothing good.

choices.why: Paul's iustificatio vitae; keep forensic making-just, not a later systematic slogan as default.
Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.
